# Key Scheme

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:KeyScheme`](gmeow-KeyScheme.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/KeyScheme>
- **Category:** class
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/trust`](../../slices/trust.md)
- **Box roles:** [TBox role](../boxes/tbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

The cryptographic scheme/format of a key (OpenPGP, X.509, SSH, Nostr, …). Modelled as a value, not a key subclass: the set of schemes is open-ended and they carry no distinct key structure here, so a new scheme is a new individual, not a new class.

## Structure

**Subclass of:** [`gufo:QualityValue`](../../external/terms.md#gufo-qualityvalue)

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:KeyScheme`](gmeow-KeyScheme.md) as a specialized kind of [`gufo:QualityValue`](../../external/terms.md#gufo-qualityvalue). Add statement metadata or a standpoint when the assertion needs provenance, confidence, or vantage.

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use as the value vocabulary behind [`gmeow:keyScheme`](../properties/gmeow-keyScheme.md) — the open set of individuals naming a key's format (OpenPGP, X.509, SSH, Nostr, …) so consumers can filter or align keys by scheme.

### Avoid when

- Avoid minting per-scheme key subclasses (schemes are individuals, not classes) and avoid using it for the key's algorithm (that is the literal [`gmeow:keyAlgorithm`](../properties/gmeow-keyAlgorithm.md), e.g. ed25519); the scheme is the format family, not the primitive.

### How to use

- Reference the seeded scheme individuals from a key via the functional [`gmeow:keyScheme`](../properties/gmeow-keyScheme.md); extend the vocabulary by adding a new [`gmeow:KeyScheme`](gmeow-KeyScheme.md) individual when a new format appears, never a subclass.

### Examples

- ex:keySchemeMinisign a [`gmeow:KeyScheme`](gmeow-KeyScheme.md); [rdfs:label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "Minisign"@en.
